## 🏄 Deta Surf - Simple Explanation

**Surf is an AI-powered notebook/browser hybrid** that lets you research and take notes without constantly switching between apps, tabs, and windows.

### The Core Idea

Imagine combining:

- 📓 A **note-taking app** (like Notion)
- 🌐 A **web browser** (like Chrome)
- 🤖 An **AI assistant** (like ChatGPT)
- 📄 A **PDF reader**

...into one app where they all talk to each other seamlessly.

### What Can It Do?

| Feature         | Example                                                               |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Smart Notes** | `@mention` a YouTube video → AI summarizes it for you                 |
| **Web Search**  | Ask "search for X" → results come into your notes                     |
| **PDF Notes**   | Open a PDF → ask questions about it                                   |
| **Surflets**    | Ask "make me a calculator app" → generates interactive mini-apps      |
| **Citations**   | AI answers link back to exact sources (timestamps, pages, paragraphs) |

### Tech Stack (Architecture)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Electron App (app/)                   │
│  ┌─────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  main/  │  │ preload/ │  │       renderer/        │  │
│  │ (Node)  │  │ (Bridge) │  │  (Svelte + TypeScript) │  │
│  └─────────┘  └──────────┘  └────────────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │
        ┌──────────────────┼──────────────────┐
        ▼                  ▼                  ▼
┌───────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐
│ @deta/backend │  │ @deta/editor │  │  @deta/services  │
│    (Rust)     │  │   (Tiptap)   │  │   (Core logic)   │
└───────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────────┘
```

**Key packages:**

- `app/` → The main Electron desktop app
- `packages/backend/` → Rust backend (compiled to Node.js module)
- `packages/services/` → Core app logic (tabs, notebooks, settings)
- `packages/editor/` → Rich text editor (Tiptap-based)
- `packages/ui/` → Reusable UI components

## 🛠️ What You Need to Run Locally

### Prerequisites

1. **Node.js** (v22.18.0 or higher)
2. **Yarn** (v1.x - classic)
3. **Rust** (with Cargo)

### Quick Start Commands

```bash
# 1. Install dependencies
yarn install

# 2. Run in development mode
yarn dev
```

That's it! The `yarn dev` command will:

- Build the Rust backend
- Compile all the TypeScript/Svelte packages
- Launch the Electron app in dev mode with hot reload

## 🤖 How AI Works in Surf

### The AI System Architecture

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Your AI Setup (pick one)                    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Option A: Bring Your Own API Key (BYOK)                       │
│  ┌──────────┐  ┌───────────┐  ┌──────────┐                     │
│  │  OpenAI  │  │ Anthropic │  │  Google  │                     │
│  │ (GPT-4o) │  │ (Claude)  │  │ (Gemini) │                     │
│  └──────────┘  └───────────┘  └──────────┘                     │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Option B: Custom/Local Models                                  │
│  ┌──────────┐  ┌────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐                 │
│  │  Ollama  │  │ OpenRouter │  │ HuggingFace │                 │
│  │ (Local)  │  │  (Cloud)   │  │   (Cloud)   │                 │
│  └──────────┘  └────────────┘  └─────────────┘                 │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Surf App (OpenAI-compatible API)                   │
│                                                                 │
│   packages/backend (Rust) ←→ packages/services (AIService)     │
│                                                                 │
│   All models talk to: /v1/chat/completions endpoint            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Built-in Model Support

Surf has **pre-configured support** for these providers/models:

| Provider           | Models                                        | What You Need            |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| **OpenAI**         | GPT-5, GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, o3-mini               | OpenAI API key           |
| **Anthropic**      | Claude 4.5/4/3.7/3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Haiku | Anthropic API key        |
| **Google**         | Gemini 2.0 Flash                              | Google AI Studio API key |
| **Ollama** (local) | Any model you download                        | Nothing (runs locally)   |
| **OpenRouter**     | 100+ models                                   | OpenRouter API key       |

---

## 🔧 What You Need to Make AI Work Locally

### Option 1: Use Cloud APIs (Easiest)

Get an API key from any of these:

- **OpenAI**: https://platform.openai.com/api-keys
- **Anthropic**: https://console.anthropic.com/settings/keys
- **Google AI**: https://aistudio.google.com/app/api-keys

Then configure it in the app: **Preferences → AI → Configure your AI Models**

### Option 2: Run AI Locally with Ollama (Free, Private)

```bash
# 1. Install Ollama (if not already installed)
brew install ollama

# 2. Start Ollama server
ollama serve

# 3. Pull a model (e.g., llama3, mistral, qwen2)
ollama pull llama3.2

# 4. In Surf settings, add a custom model:
#    Provider URL: http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions
#    Model ID: llama3.2
```

---

| Step | Requirement       | Status                    |
| ---- | ----------------- | ------------------------- |
| 1    | Node.js ≥ 22.18.0 | ✅ You have 22.20.0       |

| 3    | Rust + Cargo      | ✅ You have 1.88.0        |
| 4    | **AI Provider**   | ⚠️ **Need to choose one** |

### Quick Start Commands

```bash
# Install dependencies
yarn install

# Run the app
yarn dev
```

Then in the app, go to **Preferences → AI** and either:

- Enter your OpenAI/Anthropic/Google API key, OR
- Add a custom model (like Ollama)

My company acts as a middleware that routes our request to these models. I'll give you the configuration and sample code, and let me know how we can achieve using models from my company in the local and get this app working.

CONFIGURATIONS:

# ================================

# CREATE A FILE NAMED ".env"

# ================================

# Use the following endpoint for standard chat completions:

API_URL=https://quasarmarket.coforge.com/qag/llmrouter-api/v2/chat/completions

# Alternatively, use this endpoint for TrustAI-enabled chat completions:

API_URL=https://quasarmarket.coforge.com/qag/llmrouter-api/v3/chat/completions

MODEL_NAME=kimi-k2-thinking

# Replace with your actual API key

API_KEY=<YOUR_API_KEY>

# ================================

# CREATE A FILE NAMED "requirements.txt"

# ================================

# Install the required Python dependencies

langchain

python-dotenv

SAMPLE PYTHON CODE:

from langchain_core.language_models import LLM

from langchain_core.prompts import PromptTemplate

import requests

from typing import List, Optional

from dotenv import load_dotenv

import os

load_dotenv(override=True)

config = os.environ

class CustomLLM(LLM):

    model: str

    endpoint_url: str = config['API_URL']

    headers: dict = {

        "Content-Type": "application/json",

        "X-API-KEY": config['API_KEY']

    }

    temperature: float = 0.7

    top_p: float = 1.0

    max_tokens: int = 2000

    stream: bool = False

    stop: Optional[List[str]] = None



    def _call(self, prompt: str, stop: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> str:

        payload = {

            "model": self.model,

            "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],

            "temperature": self.temperature,

            "top_p": self.top_p,

            "max_tokens": self.max_tokens

        }

        if stop:

            payload["stop"] = stop

        response = requests.post(self.endpoint_url, headers=self.headers, json=payload)

        response.raise_for_status()

        data = response.json()

        return data['choices'][0]['message']['content']



    @property

    def _llm_type(self) -> str:

        return "custom-llm"

llm = CustomLLM(

    model=config['MODEL_NAME'],

    temperature=0.5,

    top_p=0.9,

    max_tokens=1000

)

prompt = PromptTemplate.from_template("You are helpful AI. Reply to: {text}")

if **name** == "**main**":

    user_input = prompt.format(text="What is Quantum Computing?")

    response = llm.invoke(user_input)

    print("LLM Response:", response)

```rust:251-268:packages/backend/src/ai/llm/client/mod.rs
fn get_headers(&self, api_key: Option<String>) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let mut headers = vec![("Content-Type".to_string(), "application/json".to_string())];

    if let Some(api_key) = api_key {
        let auth = match self {
            Self::OpenAI | Self::Google | Self::Custom(_) => {
                ("Authorization".to_string(), format!("Bearer {}", api_key))  // ❌ Your API needs X-API-KEY
            }
            Self::Anthropic => ("x-api-key".to_string(), api_key.to_string()),  // ✅ This is what you need!
        };
        headers.push(auth);
    }
    // ...
}
```

## 🔴 The Problem

| What Surf Sends               | What Your Company Expects |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `Authorization: Bearer <key>` | `X-API-KEY: <key>`        |

Your company's API uses **`X-API-KEY`** header (like Anthropic), but Surf sends **`Authorization: Bearer`** for custom providers.

---

## ✅ Solutions

I'll give you **two options**:

### Option 1: Quick Fix - Local Proxy (No Code Changes)

Run a tiny proxy that transforms the header. Create this file:

---

```diff
@@ -1,1 +1,97 @@
-
+ #!/usr/bin/env node
+ /**
+  * Coforge API Proxy
+  *
+  * This proxy transforms Surf's &#96;Authorization: Bearer &lt;key&gt;&#96; header
+  * into &#96;X-API-KEY: &lt;key&gt;&#96; for your company's LLM router.
+  *
+  * Usage:
+  *   1. Set your API key: export COFORGE_API_KEY="your-api-key"
+  *   2. Run: node coforge-proxy.js
+  *   3. In Surf, add custom model with URL: http://localhost:3456/v1/chat/completions
+  */
+
+ const http = require('http');
+ const https = require('https');
+
+ const PROXY_PORT = 3456;
+ const COFORGE_API_URL = 'https://quasarmarket.coforge.com/qag/llmrouter-api/v2/chat/completions';
+ const API_KEY = process.env.COFORGE_API_KEY;
+
+ if (!API_KEY) {
+   console.error('❌ Error: COFORGE_API_KEY environment variable not set');
+   console.error('   Run: export COFORGE_API_KEY="your-api-key"');
+   process.exit(1);
+ }
+
+ const server = http.createServer((req, res) =&gt; {
+   // Enable CORS
+   res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*');
+   res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Methods', 'POST, OPTIONS');
+   res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Headers', 'Content-Type, Authorization');
+
+   if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') {
+     res.writeHead(200);
+     res.end();
+     return;
+   }
+
+   if (req.method !== 'POST') {
+     res.writeHead(405, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
+     res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Method not allowed' }));
+     return;
+   }
+
+   let body = '';
+   req.on('data', chunk =&gt; { body += chunk; });
+
+   req.on('end', () =&gt; {
+     const url = new URL(COFORGE_API_URL);
+
+     const options = {
+       hostname: url.hostname,
+       port: 443,
+       path: url.pathname,
+       method: 'POST',
+       headers: {
+         'Content-Type': 'application/json',
+         'X-API-KEY': API_KEY,  // Transform header here!
+       }
+     };
+
+     console.log(&#96;📤 Proxying request to Coforge API...&#96;);
+
+     const proxyReq = https.request(options, (proxyRes) =&gt; {
+       res.writeHead(proxyRes.statusCode, proxyRes.headers);
+       proxyRes.pipe(res);
+       console.log(&#96;📥 Response: ${proxyRes.statusCode}&#96;);
+     });
+
+     proxyReq.on('error', (e) =&gt; {
+       console.error(&#96;❌ Proxy error: ${e.message}&#96;);
+       res.writeHead(500, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
+       res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: e.message }));
+     });
+
+     proxyReq.write(body);
+     proxyReq.end();
+   });
+ });
+
+ server.listen(PROXY_PORT, () =&gt; {
+   console.log(&#96;
+ ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
+ ║           🚀 Coforge API Proxy Running                        ║
+ ╠═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
+ ║  Local URL:  http://localhost:${PROXY_PORT}/v1/chat/completions       ║
+ ║  Target:     ${COFORGE_API_URL.substring(0, 50)}... ║
+ ║  Model:      kimi-k2-thinking                                 ║
+ ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
+
+ 📝 In Surf Settings → AI → Add Custom Model:
+    • Provider URL: http://localhost:${PROXY_PORT}/v1/chat/completions
+    • Model ID:     kimi-k2-thinking
+    • API Key:      (leave empty - proxy handles it)
+ &#96;);
+ });
+
```

All changes are in place! Here's the complete summary:

## ✅ Complete Solution for Coforge API Integration

I've implemented **two options** for you:

---

### Option 1: Quick Proxy (No Code Build Required)

If you want to test immediately **without rebuilding the app**:

```bash
# 1. Set your API key
export COFORGE_API_KEY="your-actual-api-key"

# 2. Run the proxy
node coforge-proxy.js
```

Then in Surf Settings → AI → Add Custom Model:
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Model Label | Kimi K2 Thinking |
| Model ID | kimi-k2-thinking |
| API Key | _(leave empty)_ |
| API Endpoint | http://localhost:3456/v1/chat/completions |

---

### Option 2: Native Support (Recommended - Requires Rebuild)

I've added native `X-API-KEY` header support to Surf. The changes:

| File                                                        | Change                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `packages/types/src/ai.types.ts`                            | Added `AuthHeaderType` enum            |
| `packages/backend/src/ai/llm/client/mod.rs`                 | Added auth header type support in Rust |
| `packages/backend/types/index.ts`                           | Added TypeScript types for backend     |
| `packages/services/src/lib/ai/ai.ts`                        | Pass auth header type to backend       |
| `app/src/renderer/Settings/components/ModelSettings.svelte` | Added UI dropdown for auth header type |

**To use this:**

```bash
# 1. Install dependencies
yarn install

# 2. Build and run
yarn dev
```

Then in Surf Settings → AI → Add Custom Model:
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Model Label | Kimi K2 Thinking |
| Model ID | kimi-k2-thinking |
| API Key | _your Coforge API key_ |
| **Auth Header Type** | **X-API-KEY Header (for Coforge, etc.)** ← NEW! |
| API Endpoint | https://quasarmarket.coforge.com/qag/llmrouter-api/v2/chat/completions |
| Context Size | 128000 |
| Supports Vision | _(check if model supports it)_ |
